assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of the active peptide to degradation-resistant agonists, produced a discrete, clearly describable change in how type 2 diabetes and obesity are treated. Originality, clarity and lasting clinical and mechanistic impact are all very strong.
assessment.attribution: Holst (secretion, physiology, human studies) and Drucker (receptor biology, intestinotrophic and cardiometabolic actions, translation) are decisive. Mojsov's work on identifying the active truncated GLP-1 peptide is an important but contested contribution. Knudsen is a drug-development figure whose recognition is less natural for a discovery prize. Credit for the early peptide discovery (e.g. Habener, Bell) is not on this list, so the configuration is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal outcomes is confirmed by large independent trials over more than a decade, so the interpretation is stable and the timing is excellent.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around the active peptide, with candidates outside the supplied credit.
Whether the committee prefers recognising the physiology or the therapeutics.
I have not independently verified the details of the credit dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and of mTOR pathways as master regulators of growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism is a conceptually unifying finding of lasting importance across cell biology, ageing, cancer and immunology.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined it as a growth regulator in yeast, which is the decisive step. Sabatini (mTOR complexes, nutrient sensing, with Sabatini's early mTOR isolation) and Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin chemistry, FRAP/mTOR) are the plausible co-recipients. The allocation is not obvious, since others such as Sabatini's and Abraham's labs overlapped.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent confirmation, and clinical use of rapalogs, make this mature, though several therapeutic applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlapping early mTOR isolation by several groups (including those not credited here).
Fair division of credit among the biochemical and genetic discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib proved that inhibiting a defining oncogenic kinase can transform a lethal cancer into a manageable disease. It founded modern targeted oncology and has had large, durable clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (medicinal and biochemical programme), Druker (clinical translation and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The upstream discovery of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore, Groffen) is outside this credit.
assessment.maturity: Twenty-plus years of follow-up give strong, independent confirmation. Recognition has been long awaited, which may raise timing questions only through prior Lasker-type recognition, not scientific doubt.
uncertainties: The role of earlier BCR-ABL discoveries not supplied in the credited names.
Whether a drug-development prize fits the committee's discovery orientation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general tool for causal control of defined cell types with light, and it changed the experimental practice of the field. The importance and originality of channelrhodopsin and its adaptation are high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterised channelrhodopsin, while Deisseroth and Boyden established its neuronal use. Miesenböck's earlier genetic photoactivation concept is a further claimant. With six names for at most three slots, allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for fifteen years, with early clinical use in vision restoration, so the method is mature even if its therapeutic uses are still emerging.
uncertainties: Difficult allocation among six credited names.
The prize is for a method rather than a disease mechanism, and the committee may judge it as a tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a living-drug modality that produces durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. The impact is large and the principle is generalisable.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June developed the costimulatory CAR designs and clinical translation, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is outside the supplied credit, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approvals and multi-year remission data support the clinical result, but long-term toxicity, solid-tumor limits and manufacturing remain open, so the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Priority of Eshhar and others not credited.
Durability and applicability beyond haematological cancers is still unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling in which the endoplasmic reticulum reports its folding load, with broad significance for secretory physiology, disease and ageing. It is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and complementarily identified the signal-transduction pathway (Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 splicing), which supports a clean two-person allocation. Others, such as Ron and Harding for PERK and ATF6 work, might also be argued, but they are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation in yeast and mammals mean the mechanism is firm. Clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Contributions of PERK/ATF6 pathway researchers not on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like-particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, and population data now show large reductions in precancer and cancer. This is major preventive medicine with a clear mechanistic basis.
assessment.attribution: Frazer, Lowy and Schiller are the usually cited originators of L1 VLP vaccine concepts and development, although Zhou, Frazer and others, and the Kirnbauer work, give a degree of overlap. zur Hausen was recognised in 2008 for the virus link to cancer, which makes a vaccine prize a different, later step.
assessment.maturity: Real-world effectiveness is now documented in several countries, with good timing, although long-term cancer endpoints are still accruing.
uncertainties: Complex priority among the groups that made the VLPs.
Possible overlap with the 2008 prize for HPV and cervical cancer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified the principal cytosolic DNA-sensing route to type I interferon and inflammatory responses, with importance for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing. It is a clear, original mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide cGAMP second messenger, and Barber identified STING. Ishikawa, Wu and Sun contributed decisively but as trainees or co-authors, and a two-person prize is the cleanest option. Others, such as Vance and Patel, are outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is firmly confirmed, but therapeutic applications are still in trials, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic effect is not yet established.
Fair attribution among the several groups in the field.
